dossiers.catalyst_stack: On April 29 and July 22, 2026, Alphabet delivered consecutive beats, culminating in Q2 revenue of $119.8 billion (+24% YoY) and Google Cloud of $24.8 billion (+82%), and it raised the dividend 5% to $0.22 in Q1. Product cadence ran from Gemini Intelligence and I/O (May 12–19) through Pixel 11 (August 12) to Gemini 4 Argon GA (October 13), while an $80 billion equity raise on June 1 and a $25 billion bond sale on August 6 funded AI infrastructure at the cost of dilution and added leverage. Regulatory drag stayed large: the EU’s top court upheld the €4.1 billion Android fine on July 2, the Commission levied €890 million in DMA penalties on July 23, Poland opened a publisher-pay probe on October 5, and Google is appealing EU Android-AI and search-data mandates as of October 15, though a U.S. judge declined to force an AdX sale on September 2. Berkshire’s August 14 13F showed a ~$37.8 billion stake and most firms lifted targets into October (Tigress/TD Cowen toward $485), leaving growth and AI execution roughly offset by financing and antitrust costs.
dossiers.key_assumption: Cloud and Gemini growth continue to justify 2026 equity/debt-funded AI capex, so dilution and DMA/Android cash fines do not re-rate the ads franchise, and September 2 behavioral ad-tech remedies remain less severe than a breakup.
